skill.name: doc-generator
skill.description: Generate Markdown documentation from Python codebases by analyzing source files, docstrings, type hints, and module structure.
skill.summary: Generate Markdown API documentation for Python projects from source files.
skill.author: bossjones

security_audit.summary: All eight static external-command findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences and inline code formatting in SKILL.md. A separate semantic risk remains because the skill recommends inspect-based runtime introspection, which can execute import-time Python code. No prompt injection, network access, or credential handling was found.

remediation.suggestion: Prefer ast parsing for documentation. Use inspect only on trusted code or inside an isolated environment with no secrets or network access.

semantic_findings.title: Runtime Introspection May Execute Source Code
semantic_findings.description: SKILL.md recommends AST or inspection and the inspect module for runtime introspection. If an agent imports untrusted Python to inspect it, import-time side effects can run.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The file explicitly recommends inspect-based runtime introspection, which commonly requires imports. The skill also allows AST parsing, so risk depends on implementation and user context.

content.value_statement: Python projects often lack consistent API documentation. This skill turns source files, docstrings, and type hints into organized Markdown documentation.
actual_capabilities: Creates Markdown documentation for Python files and directories.
Extracts module, class, function, and method docstrings.
Includes type hints and function signatures in reference sections.
Organizes modules, classes, methods, and functions into readable sections.
Handles missing docstrings by noting absent descriptions.
limitations: Documentation quality depends on available docstrings and type hints.
Files with syntax errors may be skipped with a warning.
Generated examples may need human review before publication.

use_cases.title: Create API References
use_cases.description: Generate module, class, and function documentation for a Python library release.

use_cases.title: Draft Project READMEs
use_cases.description: Turn source structure and docstrings into a clear README starting point.

use_cases.title: Document Internal Services
use_cases.description: Produce consistent Markdown documentation for internal Python modules and service utilities.

prompt_templates.title: Document One File
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a single module.
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate Markdown documentation for this Python file. Include classes, functions, parameters, returns, and usage notes.

prompt_templates.title: Build A Module Reference
prompt_templates.prompt: Create API documentation for this Python package. Group content by module, then list classes, methods, and functions.

prompt_templates.title: Improve Existing Docs
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the current Markdown documentation against the Python source. Update missing signatures, docstrings, and return details.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare Release Documentation
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate release-ready API documentation for this Python project. Add a table of contents, usage examples, and missing-docstring warnings.

output_examples.input: A Python utility module with functions and type hints.
output_examples.output: A Markdown module page with a summary, function reference, parameter details, return descriptions, and usage notes.

output_examples.input: A package directory containing classes, methods, and docstrings.
output_examples.output: A structured API reference grouped by module, with class sections, method signatures, and docstring summaries.

output_examples.input: A project with sparse docstrings and missing type hints.
output_examples.output: A documentation draft that marks missing descriptions and highlights areas needing author review.

best_practices: Provide the project root or exact Python files to document.
Review generated descriptions for accuracy before publishing.
Keep docstrings current so generated documentation stays useful.
anti_patterns: Do not use it for non-Python projects.
Do not publish generated documentation without source owner review.
Do not expect complete examples when source files lack examples.

faq.question: Does this skill execute my Python code?
faq.answer: The skill recommends static parsing first and does not require external dependencies for basic documentation generation.

faq.question: Can it document a full package?
faq.answer: Yes. It can process a directory and organize documentation by module, class, method, and function.

faq.question: What formats does it generate?
faq.answer: It generates Markdown documentation suitable for READMEs, API references, and internal project docs.

faq.question: How does it handle missing docstrings?
faq.answer: It notes missing descriptions and continues generating the remaining documentation.

faq.question: Does it support type hints?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes type hints and signatures when they are present in the source.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, or Claude Code use it?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
